arxiv-2103-14460.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Christian Hansen, Casper Hansen, Jakob Grue Simonsen, Stephen Alstrup, Christina Lioma. Semantic hashing represents documents as compact binary vectors (hash codes) and allows both efficient and effective similarity search in large-scale information retrieval. The state of the art has primarily focused on learning hash codes that improve similarity search effectiveness, while assuming a brute-force linear scan strategy for searching over all the hash codes, even though much faster alternatives exist.

arxiv-2210-07971.title: Hamilton’s equations in the covariant teleparallel equivalent of general relativity
arxiv-2210-07971.creator: Laxmipriya Pati, Daniel Blixt, María-José Guzmán
arxiv-2210-07971.description: Abstract We present Hamilton’s equations for the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR), which is a reformulation of general relativity based on a curvatureless, metric compatible, and torsionful connection. For this, we consider the Hamiltonian for TEGR obtained through the vector, antisymmetric, symmetric and trace-free, and trace irreducible decomposition of the phase space variables.

arxiv-2305-02320.title: Generating Synthetic Documents for Cross-Encoder Re-Rankers: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Human Experts Conference: ; May 3rd, 2023;
arxiv-2305-02320.creator: Arian Askari, Mohammad Aliannejadi, Evangelos Kanoulas, Suzan Verberne
arxiv-2305-02320.description: Abstract . We investigate the usefulness of generative Large Language Models (LLMs) in generating training data for cross-encoder re-rankers in a novel direction: generating synthetic documents instead of synthetic queries. We introduce a new dataset, ChatGPT-RetrievalQA, and compare the effectiveness of models fine-tuned on LLMgenerated and human-generated data.

arxiv-2402-13182.title: Order-Optimal Regret in Distributed Kernel Bandits using Uniform Sampling with Shared Randomness
arxiv-2402-13182.creator: Nikola Pavlovic, Sudeep Salgia, Qing Zhao
arxiv-2402-13182.description: Abstract We consider distributed kernel bandits where N N agents aim to collaboratively maximize an unknown reward function that lies in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Each agent sequentially queries the function to obtain noisy observations at the query points.

The recent development of various Bioinformatics toolkits has facilitated the rapid processing and analysis of vast quantities of biological data for human perception.

arxiv-2407-02000.title: Sub-millisecond electric field sensing with an individual rare-earth doped ferroelectric nanocrystal
arxiv-2407-02000.creator: Athulya K. Muraleedharan, Jingye Zou, Maxime Vallet, Abdelali Zaki, Christine Bogicevic, Charles Paillard, Karen Perronet, François Treussart
arxiv-2407-02000.description: Abstract Understanding the dynamics of electrical signals within neuronal assemblies is crucial to unraveling complex brain function. Despite recent advances in employing optically active nanostructures in transmembrane potential sensing, there remains room for improvement in terms of response time and sensitivity.

arxiv-2410-03883.title: DiSK : Differentially Private Optimizer with Simplified Kalman Filter for Noise Reduction
arxiv-2410-03883.creator: Xinwei Zhang, Zhiqi Bu, Borja Balle, Mingyi Hong, Meisam Razaviyayn, Vahab Mirrokni
arxiv-2410-03883.description: Abstract Differential privacy (DP) offers a robust framework for safeguarding individual data privacy. To utilize DP in training modern machine learning models, differentially private optimizers have been widely used in recent years. A popular approach to privatize an optimizer is to clip the individual gradients and add sufficiently large noise to the clipped gradient.

arxiv-2507-01013.title: Running Quantum Computers in Discovery Mode
arxiv-2507-01013.creator: Benedikt Placke, G. J. Sreejith, Alessio Lerose, S. L. Sondhi
arxiv-2507-01013.description: Abstract We propose using quantum computers in conjunction with classical machine learning to discover instances of interesting quantum many-body dynamics. Concretely, an “interest function” is defined for a given circuit (family) instance that can be evaluated on a quantum computer. The circuit is then adapted by a classical learning agent to maximize interest.

pmc-11710523.title: ASSESSING DYNAMIC AFFECT RECOGNITION FOR DISTINGUISHING FRONTOTEMPORAL DEMENTIA SUBTYPES
pmc-11710523.creator: Hulya Ulugut
pmc-11710523.description: BackgroundRecent international work suggests that more precise subtyping within frontotemporal dementia (FTD) syndromes leads to better prediction of pathology, supporting individualized disease‐specific treatments. Recent studies emphasize that identification of one such subtype, semantic behavioral variant FTD (sbvFTD), relies in part on measuring emotion recognition abilities.

pmc-12439379.title: A standing wave tube-like setup designed for tomographic imaging of the sound-induced motion patterns in fish hearing structures
pmc-12439379.creator: Isabelle P Maiditsch, Tanja Schulz-Mirbach, Martin Heß, Friedrich Ladich, Marco Stampanoni, Christian M Schlepütz
pmc-12439379.description: BackgroundModern bony fishes exhibit a considerable variation in the morphology of their hearing structures, and the morphological composition of these has been studied for centuries. However, the precise interaction and contribution of individual structures to hearing remains unclear in many species.

pmc-12549821.creator: Xianfu Zhou, Lihong Lin, Yali Zhan, Xiaoyang Li, Mengmeng Zhou
pmc-12549821.description: This study aimed to evaluate the attitudes and practices of healthcare professionals at a comprehensive tertiary hospital regarding the use of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) in influenza treatment. A cross-sectional survey was conducted at Quzhou Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between June 5 and July 14, 2024.

pmc-12584527.title: Non-linear relationship between the triglyceride glucose-a body shape index and stroke risk: a prospective cohort study from the China health and retirement longitudinal study
pmc-12584527.creator: Dongpo He, Zhenzhen Fan, Xintao Zhang, Changchun Cao, Yong Han, Haofei Hu, Xiaodan Zheng
pmc-12584527.description: ObjectiveRecent evidence suggests a strong association between triglyceride glucose-a body shape index (TyG-ABSI) and cardiovascular mortality. However, the association between TyG-ABSI and incident stroke has not been explored. Our study utilized a prospective cohort design to explore the potential association between TyG-ABSI and incident stroke within a Chinese population.

pmc-12646490.title: Conservative Management of Atrioventricular Groove Hematoma in Mitral Valve Repair Surgery: A Case Report
pmc-12646490.creator: Xia Zhang, Yangzhao Zhou, Zhaoshun Yuan, Jianming Li, Kang Zhou
pmc-12646490.description: An accidental injury to the myocardial tissue below the posterior annulus occurred during mitral valve repair surgery, leading to the formation of an atrioventricular groove hematoma. By evaluating the size of the communication orifice and monitoring the bleeding tendency, we successfully managed the complication conservatively, thus preventing cardiac rupture and the necessity for reoperation.

pmc-13067548.creator: Dan Zhu, Fei Ying, Liping Wei, Xiaolong He

pmc-13127424.title: Emergent latent neurotoxic effects of manganese following nominal chronic exposures in human stem cell and Caenorhabditis elegans models
pmc-13127424.creator: Xueqi Tang, Airton C Martins, Anke M Tukker, Hyunjin Kim, Michael Aschner, Aaron B Bowman
pmc-13127424.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Behavioral deficits can emerge after the removal of manganese (Mn) exposures in humans and other mammals. Although epidemiological studies provide substantial evidence supporting latency, challenges reproducing such effects in alternative models have slowed mechanistic understanding. Here, we report in 2 systems, human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived and Caenorhabditis elegans, that prior chronic exposure elicits clear latent neurotoxic effects in gene expression and functional outcomes.

pmc-13354194.title: Learning from COVID-19: clinical trials, health information technology, and patient mortality
pmc-13354194.creator: Christos Nicolaides, Avinash Collis, Seth Benzell, Indranil Bardhan
pmc-13354194.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, deaths per case in the United States decreased from 7.46% in April 2020 to 1.76% in April 2021. One mechanism that could explain this decline is a learning effect associated with testing of new treatments by hospitals. Hospitals that participated in clinical trials developed better organizational capabilities to diagnose and treat COVID-19 patients.

pmc-13629232.title: A resurrection experiment reveals reduced adaptive potential in a common agricultural weed
pmc-13629232.creator: Sasha G D Bishop, John R Stinchcombe, Regina S Baucom
pmc-13629232.description: Adaptive evolution is critical to population responses under accelerating anthropogenic global change. Although theory and some empirical work suggest that contemporary rates of environmental change can be met by equally rapid evolutionary shifts, mismatches between expected and realized evolution remain common in natural systems.
